Contributing to regcompR

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for considering a contribution to regcompR. The package is a statistical tool, so a change is judged on two things: whether the R code is sound, and whether its numbers agree with an independent reference.

Before You Start

  • Use GitHub issues for bug reports, feature requests, documentation gaps, and requests for new distributions or models.
  • For larger changes, such as a new engine or a family of distributions, open an issue first so the design can be discussed before implementation.
  • Keep pull requests focused. A new family, a bug fix, and a refactor should usually be separate pull requests.

Reporting a Wrong Answer

A wrong result is the most valuable bug report. Please include:

  • a reproducible R snippet (simulated data is fine),
  • what regcompR returns,
  • what a reference implementation returns for the same model (for example stats, lme4, glmmTMB, gamlss, VGAM, MASS, ordinal or survival), if you can run it,
  • sessionInfo().

Development Setup

Install the development dependencies from the repository root:

install.packages(c("remotes", "testthat", "devtools", "roxygen2"))
remotes::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)

regcompR has no compiled code of its own. The TMB engine needs RTMB; the Bayesian engines need a Stan runner (cmdstanr, rstan or bayescompR), JAGS with R2jags, or OpenBUGS with R2OpenBUGS.

Adding a Distribution

  • Register the family with family_def() and register_family() in the matching R/zfam-*.R file: parameters with their domains and links, the log density, and the distribution function, quantile, random generation and moments where they exist, with the conditions under which moments exist.
  • Cite a primary source for the density and its parameterization.
  • Add a test that checks normalization and compares the density, distribution function and moments with a reference package or with simulation. Do not write an expected value by hand when a reference can produce it.
  • Give the family a Stan density where one can be written, so the Bayesian engine supports it.

Adding a Model or Engine Feature

  • Validate estimates, standard errors and the log likelihood against an established package on simulated and real data, and keep that comparison as a test (skipped when the reference package is not installed).
  • Keep results identical across engines where the model is the same.

Branches and Pull Requests

  • Use one branch per logical change, named after the change (add-sichel-family, fix-ordinal-prediction).
  • Write commit subjects in the imperative (“Add the Sichel family”).
  • Keep the implementation, its tests, the roxygen source, the regenerated documentation, and the NEWS.md bullet together in the same pull request.

Code Style

  • Follow the style already used in the surrounding R files.
  • Prefer clear validation and explicit errors over silent coercion; use the condition helpers in R/conditions.R.
  • Work on the log scale for densities and use the stable helpers (log_sum_exp(), log1mexp(), log1pexp()).
  • Do not add new package dependencies unless they are necessary and justified.
  • Regenerate the .Rd files with devtools::document() after changing roxygen comments.

Testing

Run the tests while developing:

devtools::test()

Before a pull request, run the full check:

R CMD build .
R CMD check --as-cran regcompR_*.tar.gz

Pull Request Checklist

Before opening a pull request, confirm:

  • Tests relevant to the change pass, with expected values from a reference.
  • Documentation is updated.
  • NEWS.md has an entry for user-facing changes.
  • No generated build artifacts, local caches, .Rcheck directories, or tarballs are committed.

Code of Conduct

All contributors are expected to follow the project Code of Conduct.
